purpose: Agent-readable catalog for selecting circular watch-face widgets before rendering them on a webpage.

source.canonicalReference: Figma components are the visual reference, but webpage generation must use circular-widget-visual-specs.json for SVG/CSS construction.

globalRules.rule: When generating webpage UI, choose a component from this catalog and render it using the matching entry in circular-widget-visual-specs.json.
Circular widgets must use exactly one declared size token. Do not stretch or scale a gauge to arbitrary dimensions.

Circular gauge colors must be resolved by watch-face-generation-rules.md. Close Gauge consumes one widget_accent_color. Open Gauge consumes either one widget_accent_color or two rule-selected colors for its component-specific gradient behavior.

components.semanticUse: A compact circular progress widget for one metric with a single current value, such as activity progress, battery, hydration, focus, completion, calories, or any bounded scalar status.

value.description: Primary value displayed in the center of the gauge.

label.description: Short secondary label below the value. Keep to one short word when possible.

icon.description: Icon rendered in the center of the gauge.

progress.description: Normalized progress used to draw the value arc.

metricKind.description: Optional semantic hint for fallback demo colors only. Production color selection must use widget_accent_color from watch-face-generation-rules.md.

selectionGuidance: Use when the user needs one glanceable metric rather than a comparison.
Use property=text when the numeric value is important.
Use property=icon when the value can be represented by a familiar icon and space is tight.
Prefer size S or M for secondary widgets and size L for the main supporting widget.

components.semanticUse: An open-arc circular widget for metrics that benefit from range, threshold, comparison, or offset context, such as temperature, heart rate zone, UV index, air quality, recovery, pace, or high/low values.

value.description: Current or primary value displayed in the center.

label.description: Short secondary label for text-only open gauges.

min.description: Lower bound used to normalize measured-dot position on the open arc.

max.description: Upper bound used to normalize measured-dot position on the open arc.

lowLabel.description: Visible low value label. Usually matches min.

highLabel.description: Visible high value label. Usually matches max.

referenceValue.description: Secondary comparison value displayed near the bottom of the gauge.

measuredValue.description: Numeric value that determines the measured-dot position. Defaults to value when omitted.

referenceMeasuredValue.description: Optional numeric comparison value that determines the second measured-dot position.

metricKind.description: Optional semantic hint for fallback demo colors only. Production color selection must use widget_accent_color or the two-color open gauge rule from watch-face-generation-rules.md.

selectionGuidance: Use property=range for metrics with a meaningful low/high span, such as today's temperature low and high.
Use property=offset for current-versus-reference comparisons, such as current temperature versus feels-like, recovery versus baseline, or pace versus target.
Use property=text for a single expressive value when the open arc style better matches the composition.
Use property=icon only when the icon is immediately recognizable.
Prefer size M or L for range and offset variants because they contain multiple text values.

measuredDotBehavior.rule: Every dot named measure in the Figma component must be rendered dynamically on the webpage. Its position must correspond to the measured numeric value normalized within min and max.

rangeExample.expectedDotPosition: right edge of the open gauge ring
